kolibrios.name: KolibriOS (latest nightly)
kolibrios.notes: KolibriOS, a whole graphical OS in assembly that boots in seconds from a ~100 MB CD. vmctl downloads the latest nightly (latest-iso.7z, a rolling name) and extracts kolibri.iso; no hash is pinned because the nightly is rebuilt under the same file name and builds.kolibrios.org's sha256sums.txt did not match the file it served (2026-09-26). vmctl provision kolibrios boots the live CD straight to its desktop in about 12 s (the e1000 network comes up by itself, verified 2026-09-26); it runs from RAM, and the disk is there for its own HDD installer (FAT32). No unattended install and no SSH.

redox.name: Redox OS 0.9.0 (desktop, live)

logins.note: the login screen has it filled in

redox.notes: Redox OS 0.9.0, a microkernel OS written in Rust, desktop live image. vmctl downloads the .iso.zst from static.redox-os.org, checks it against the SHA256SUM published next to it (iso_archive.sha256) and unpacks it with zstd. vmctl provision redox boots it: the bootloader first lists the display modes and waits (Enter keeps the best one, 1280x800 here), then the graphical login has user already filled in and an empty password; the Orbital desktop follows (verified 2026-09-26, about 50 s). The disk is for Redox's own installer; no unattended install and no SSH yet.

menuetos.name: MenuetOS 64 (your CD image)
menuetos.iso_help:
MenuetOS 64 is freeware distributed only from its own site, after you accept its license (m64l.txt), through Google Drive links that change with every release: vmctl cannot download it for you.

1. Open https://www.menuetos.net/download.htm and read the license.
2. Download the CD image, M64CD-<version>.ISO (about 80 MB, 'bootable CD'), then boot it with vmctl provision menuetos.
menuetos.notes: MenuetOS 64, a 64-bit OS written entirely in assembly (GUI, SMP, networking). The medium is yours to download (see iso_help): no public stable URL, a license to accept, no checksum published. vmctl provision menuetos boots the CD; it runs from RAM. No unattended install and no SSH.

serenityos.name: SerenityOS (built from source)

logins.note: logged in already; su gives root without a password

disk_image.help:
SerenityOS publishes no ISO or disk image: it is built from source, and the build installs a GCC 14 toolchain, runs for 1-3 hours and needs root for the loop devices of the image step. Do it in a throwaway builder VM, not on the host:

1. Install an Ubuntu 22.04+ or Debian 12+ VM (vmctl bootstrap-unattended ubuntu-26.04, or any Linux VM with 4+ vCPUs, 8+ GB of RAM and 40 GB of disk).
2. Copy tools/build_serenityos.sh into it and run: sudo sh build_serenityos.sh ~/serenity-build cccf3076aacd936569f1136c6a4523b1a32a2597
3. Copy the resulting serenityos-grub-cccf3076.img back to this host (scp, or the shared folder).

Then: vmctl prep serenityos converts it into the VM's disk, vmctl start serenityos boots it. docs/SERENITYOS.md records the whole build as it was done, with the traps.

serenityos.notes: SerenityOS, a Unix-like graphical OS with its own kernel, libraries and browser, built from source at a pinned commit (see disk_image.help and tools/build_serenityos.sh; commit cccf3076 of 2026-09-26). The image is raw MBR + GRUB; vmctl prep serenityos turns it into the disk, and it boots straight to the desktop and a Terminal as user anon in about 15 s (q35, AHCI, e1000, standard VGA; verified 2026-09-26). No installer, no unattended flow, no SSH.
